items.title: Removing the first descent from a two-row standard Young tableau is a bijection
items.author: Avichai Marmor
items.work: Schur-positivity of short chords in matchings
items.difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the labelled lemma `lem:remove first descent from syt` at source lines 459-466: for integers k_1 >= k_2 >= 0 and a set J contained in [k_1+k_2-1], the number of two-row standard Young tableaux of shape (k_1,k_2) whose descent set contains J equals the number of such tableaux of shape (k_1+1,k_2+1) whose descent set contains {1} union (J+2). The author's proof (source lines 467-469) is a single paragraph, but it is an explicit bijection rather than a counting argument: the map shifts every entry by 2 and inserts a leftmost column carrying 1 and 2 (line 468), and the proof has to verify three separate properties of this map, namely injectivity, the fact that the image is again a standard Young tableau with the required descent condition, and the fact that the construction can be read backwards to recover any tableau of the larger shape with that descent condition. The statement gives only the resulting cardinality identity, and the shape of the inserted column is what the reader has to discover.
